key_idea: Only relative shifts matter: precompute for each pair of wheels which cyclic offsets are conflict-free (O(n^2) each), then try all (i,j) offset pairs in O(1) each.
sketch: Fix wheel 1 and let wheels 2 and 3 have offsets i and j. Precompute ok12[k], ok13[k], ok23[k] = no column clashes at relative shift k, each in O(n^2) with early exit. A pair (i,j) is valid iff ok12[i], ok13[j] and ok23[(j-i) mod n]. The minimum number of rotations to realise offsets (0,i,j) is the smallest range max-min over the representations i or i-n, j or j-n (sum of distances to the median of three points on the cycle). Total O(n^2) = 25M steps for n=5000. Pitfalls: orientation of the 2-3 shift, and trying to bitset/FFT when plain O(n^2) is enough.
